definitions.gloss: Roman letters, romaji, the Latin alphabet
definitions.explanation: The Latin alphabet (A-Z) used to write Japanese phonetically. Also refers to the romanization system itself.

examples.japanese: {名前|なまえ}をローマ{字|じ}で{書|か}く。
examples.english: Write your name in Roman letters.

examples.japanese: パスポートにはローマ{字|じ}で{氏名|しめい}が{記載|きさい}される。
examples.english: Names are written in Roman letters on passports.

examples.japanese: ローマ{字|じ}{入力|にゅうりょく}とかな{入力|にゅうりょく}のどちらを{使|つか}っていますか。
examples.english: Do you use romaji input or kana input?

notes:
ローマ{字|じ} literally means "Roman characters" and refers to the Latin alphabet as used to represent Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ローマ{字|じ}で{書|か}く: to write in romaji
- ローマ{字|じ}{入力|にゅうりょく}: romaji input (typing method)
- ローマ{字|じ}{表記|ひょうき}: romaji notation

ROMANIZATION SYSTEMS:
There are several romanization systems, including {訓令式|くんれいしき} (Kunrei-shiki, taught in Japanese schools) and ヘボン{式|しき} (Hepburn, used on passports and signs). Hepburn is the most widely recognized internationally.

NOTE:
Most Japanese people type using ローマ{字|じ}{入力|にゅうりょく}, where they type romanized letters that are automatically converted to kana.
